subjects.label: Parry and deflection timing
subjects.description: The Sekiro-style deflect at the centre of the fighting: the rhythm and high of a clean parry, the tightness of the timing window, the parry tutorial, unbounded talismans and counters, and jokes about parrying things outside the game; not how hard an individual boss is and not the movement or platforming.

subjects.label: Named bosses and their patterns
subjects.description: Individual boss fights as remembered encounters: Eigong above all, plus Yingzhao, Jiequan, Fuxi and Nuwa, learning a pattern over hours or days, calls to nerf or buff one, the derivations off a single move, and the death-Sol recovery inside a fight; not the parry system itself and not a general statement that the game is hard.

subjects.label: Taoist thought and Chinese myth
subjects.description: The Taoist and mythological substance players argue with: cultivation and cyber-immortality, wu wei and non-action, whether the game calls Taoism superstition, the Houyi solar myth retold, and the arc from revenge to acceptance stated as philosophy; not the cast as characters and not general praise for the writing.

subjects.label: The cast by name and gifts for Shuanshuan
subjects.description: Attachment to specific characters named in the review: bringing Shuanshuan toys and wanting more trinkets to give him, missing Heng, Lady Ethereal, Jiequan, Yi as an arrogant drunk, and roll-calls of the whole cast; not the philosophy they voice and not the volume of dialogue.

subjects.label: Cat-people design and finding them attractive
subjects.description: The Solarians as anthropomorphic cats and what players want from that: sphinx-cat and white-cat jokes, furry framing, openly fancying Jiequan or the mechanical soldiers, and requests for outfit skins; not affection for a character as a person in the story and not the art style in general.

subjects.label: Measured against Hollow Knight and Silksong
subjects.description: Reviews that name Hollow Knight or Silksong specifically: this as the metroidvania to play while Silksong does not exist, found-my-Silksong and Silksong-delay jokes, better than Hollow Knight except for the animation, and warnings that it is far more combat than exploration; not a bare statement that this is a metroidvania or a soulslike.

subjects.label: Dialogue volume and unskippable cutscenes
subjects.description: How much talking sits between the fights and whether you can get past it: interminable rambling conversations in the opening hours, cutscenes and story that cannot be skipped on a repeat run, and hating the amount of reading; not the quality of the plot or the themes it carries.

subjects.label: Map screen, fast travel and backtracking
subjects.description: Getting around Fusang: a detailed map that will not fit on one screen, save points that cannot teleport to one another, too much re-running of old ground, and guidance so thin you do not know what you are missing; not the platforming moves themselves and not the amount of content.
